cases.name: suite_selection_follows_payer_preference_not_identifier
cases.why: suite identifiers encode no preference. P-256 (2) exists only because iOS's Secure Enclave holds no Ed25519 key — a hardware-forced fallback, not an upgrade — so 'highest wins' would select the weaker option on every dual-capable pair.

cases.name: version_selection_is_highest_mutual
cases.why: versions, unlike suites, are ordered by construction: higher means newer

cases.name: no_common_suite
cases.why: the only offered suite is one this client will not speak

cases.name: downgrade_stripped_suite_fails_commitment
cases.why: a MITM removes the strong suite so the payer sees a menu of one. offer_commit covers the whole FullOffer, so the substitution is caught BEFORE any suite is chosen — negotiating first would mean selecting from an attacker-chosen menu and only then noticing.

cases.name: commitments_are_domain_separated_by_purpose
cases.why: the same canonical bytes must produce a different digest per role, so a commitment computed for one purpose cannot be presented as another
